draft.title: Director, Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology
draft.position_summary: The position, Director, Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology is a combined managerial, curatorial, and public relations role responsible for SFU’s archaeological and ethnographic collections and their presentation to the public and the University community. The Director provides vision and leadership for the Museum of Archaeology and Ethnology and oversees all museum programmes and operations including management of the Museum budget. The incumbent develops and implements the Museum’s five year plan in concert with that of the Department of Archaeology. This includes setting priorities, policies, and procedures, in accordance with international professional, scholarly, and ethical standards. The Director manages, conserves, and enlarges the Museum’s assets through interaction with public donors, staff in University Advancement, Office of the VP Academic, Office of Aboriginal Peoples, SFU Art Galleries, and the Library, as well as university faculty, staff, students, and members of the general public. The Director oversees the activities of museum staff, researchers, research associates, volunteers, work study students, interns, student assistants, and others who use Museum collections and resources. In doing this the Director ensures these individuals are working in compliance with international conventions, federal and provincial legislation, and University policies and procedures. The Director enhances the Museum’s and the University’s community engagement by establishing and maintaining a network of internal and external contacts and providing advice to small community museums.

model.title: Director, Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology
model.position_summary: The Director provides strategic vision, leadership and overall management for the Museum of Archaeology & Ethnology, ensuring its collections, programs and public presence support the university’s research, teaching and community‑engagement missions.  The role directs acquisition, conservation, exhibition and outreach activities, secures and administers diverse funding streams, and ensures compliance with international, federal and provincial heritage legislation.  By fostering internal and external partnerships, guiding staff, volunteers and students, and overseeing operational and capital projects, the Director advances the museum’s five‑year strategic plan and upholds professional, scholarly and ethical standards.
